# 🪄 dsh-photo-skins
中文 | English
Import once. Auto-accent once. Turn any photo into a skin for the DSH Web GUI.

Photo skins for the DSH Web GUI: import your own photos and turn them into
the interface skin. The p

hoto paints the backdrop behind the GUI, and the
accent colors are extracted from the photo automati

cally (dominant color as
the accent, photo-tinted light/dark readability veils). Rendering controls:

fit (cover/contain), blur (0-100px, global or split empty/content), dim
(0-100%) and the auto-accen

er/contain), blur (0-100px, global or split empty/content), dim
(0-100%) and the auto-accent toggle.

## ✨ Core Feature
### 📥 Import photos three ways

- File picker, drag-and-drop, or paste — pick whichever you like
- Supports PNG / JPG / WebP / GIF,

drag-and-drop, or paste — pick whichever you like
- Supports PNG / JPG / WebP / GIF, up to 25MB each

### 👗 Try on / apply / remove
- Manage everything from the first-level "Photo skins" settings sectio

n
- "Try on" previews temporarily without touching the applied photo
- "Apply" writes the skin in on
e click; "Remove" clears the local copy

### 🎨 Automatic accent extraction
- The photo's dominant color becomes the interface accent
- Derive

s light/dark scrim tints so the readability veils pick up the photo's own tone
- Exposes CSS variabl
es `--dsw-photo-accent` / `--dsw-photo-accent-soft` / `--dsw-photo-accent-contrast`
### 🖼️ Rendering controls

- Fit: cover / contain
- Blur: 0–100px, global or split
- Dim: 0–100%, keeping foreground content re

adable
- Accent-from-photo: toggle on/off anytime

### 💾 Local persistence
- The applied photo persists through the `photo-skins` settings namespace an

tence
- The applied photo persists through the `photo-skins` settings namespace and survives reloads

## Storage

Photos are stored under `<DSH_HOME>/photo-skins/<id>/` (`original.<ext>` plus
a `manifest.json` with

the display name, type, size and import time). Nothing
is uploaded or shared; removal deletes the l

ay name, type, size and import time). Nothing

## Web-Reach

Web-Reach is in the same plugin and free to use. It wires "web search" into DSH's web capability
sea

m (`ctx.web`) and additionally registers two native tools that the Agent
calls automatically during
a conversation when it needs current information:

- `web_search`: contributed as one of three `ctx.web` search providers —
DuckDuckGo (no key; scrapin

g-based, needs a reachable network path to
duckduckgo.com), Exa free (hosted MCP; the default backen

d, marked
"recommended" in the card), or Exa API key (requires a saved key).
- `web_fetch`: Jina Rea

der turns any public page into Markdown (no key).
- `rss_fetch`: parses an RSS 2.0 / Atom feed into
its entries (no key).

Web search is a master switch: the "Web search" toggle above the composer shows
the active backend a

nd turns it on/off, sharing the same `web-reach` namespace
as the card so the two stay in sync. When

enabled (the default), the plugin
points `ctx.web`'s `searchProviderId` at the chosen backend. when
disabled, the official DeepSeek-native search is restored.

The key entry only appears for the "Exa API key" mode. The key is stored in the
`web-reach` settings

namespace as a secret, redacted on the wire and never read
back by the browser (write-only). Search

queries and page URLs are sent to
third-party services (DuckDuckGo / Exa / Jina Reader) — the data

leaves this
machine. See Security model below.
## 🔒 Security model

- All routes (`/api/photo-skins/*`) sit behind a same-origin fence
(Sec-Fetch-Site / Origin): cross-

site webpages cannot read, import or
delete your photos.
- Uploads are validated by file magic bytes

, not by name or declared
content-type — a renamed SVG or executable is rejected (415). SVG is
delib

erately unsupported (script risk).
- Uploads are capped at 25MB (413) and written atomically (tmp +

rename).
- Stored ids are generated and validated against a whitelist regex, so no
path can escape t

he store directory.
- Web-Reach search providers and tools run in the host process (there is no
brow

ser-exposed route), and every outbound fetch is SSRF-gated: only public
http(s) URLs are fetched, an

d loopback / link-local / private / reserved IP
ranges, plus cloud-metadata hostnames and IP-obfusca

tion forms, are refused.
Redirects are re-validated and capped; responses are timeout-bounded (15-20

s)
and size-capped (2 MiB); provider/tool execution honours the turn's
cancellation signal. The Exa

hosted-MCP endpoint
(https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp) passes the same SSRF gate.
- The DuckDuckGo search path

sends only a text query term (never a URL) and
reports the decoded result URLs back without fetchin

g them.
- The Exa API key is an optional `role('secret')` settings field: stripped at
the wire bound

ary, the browser never receives the plaintext; the provider
reads it only host-side at execution tim

e. Choosing "Exa API key" without a
saved key leaves that provider unavailable and search fails loud

ly rather
than silently downgrading.
- Exa free (MCP) uses Exa's official hosted MCP endpoint, curre

ntly advertised
as keyless; its keyless status is not verified by this plugin and may change.
